To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
LSI decreases the excitatory drive onto inhibitory interneuron terminals, thereby decreasing the excitation-inhibition balance in the BLA.
limited sucrose intake increases the excitatory drive of inhibitory interneuron inputs and decreases excitatory synaptic transmission onto BLA principal neurons.
a history of palatable food consumption increases the excitation– inhibition balance in the BLA by increasing the excitability of GABAergic interneurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neurobiological underpinnings of the stress-reducing effects of palatable food.
the neural mechanisms that mediate the dampening of the HPA axis by palatable food consumption.
how the brain responds to palatable foods and their effects on the stress response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

palatable food intake blunts HPA responses by increasing the excitability of BLA parvalbumin-expressing interneurons and decreasing the probability that glutamate is released onto BLA principal neurons.
LSI increases GABAergic and decreases glutamatergigic inputs to BLA neurons, which may contribute to the dampening of the stress HPA response.
palatable food intake decreases the probability of glutamatergically mediated excitation of BLA neurons and increases the excitatory drive on BLA inhibitory neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
palatable food intake can be rewarding and can also decrease the stress response.
the consumption of palatable food can have anxiolytic-like effects, at least in part, by increasing GABAergic tone and reducing the excitability of the amygdala.
palatable food blunts the stress response through a decrease in BLA output.
The main takeaway from our work is that
palatable foods can induce plasticity in brain regions that regulate stress responses.
LSI increases the excitatory drive of inhibitory interneuronal activity in the BLA, which is a mechanism by which LSI may dampen stress-induced HPA responses.
palatable food intake can alter the brain in ways that are similar to stress.
